title: Generic For Loops
summary: `for k, v in source do ... end` walks whatever a source yields: array elements, dictionary pairs, players, tagged instances. In Luau, built-in tables can be iterated directly.

syntax: for i, v in pairs(t) do end        -- all key/value pairs (any order)
for i, v in ipairs(arr) do end     -- array part, 1..n in order
for i, v in arr do end             -- Luau: direct iteration = ipairs
for k, v in next, t do end         -- explicit next-based walk
for player in Players:GetPlayers() do end  -- arrays from APIs work too

details.heading: Iterator protocol
details.body: The `in` clause takes an iterator function plus its state. `pairs`, `ipairs`, `string.gmatch`, and custom generators all fit. Roblox APIs that return arrays can be iterated directly in Luau.

details.heading: Loop variables are per-iteration
details.body: In Luau (unlike classic Lua), each iteration gets its own copy of the loop variables — closing over them in callbacks behaves intuitively.

explanation.whatItIs: The 'walk through everything' loop. You don't manage indices by hand — the source hands you each entry.
explanation.whyItExists: Iterating collections is the most common loop; generic for makes it one line and impossible to off-by-one.
whenToUse: `for i, v in array` for ordered lists
`for k, v in pairs(dict)` for named entries
`for word in text:gmatch("%S+")` for pattern matches
whenNotToUse: Don't mutate the array you're iterating (adding/removing) — iterate a copy or walk indices backwards with a numeric for
Don't use `pairs` when order matters — it guarantees none
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local pets = {"Cat", "Dog", "Dragon"}

for i, v in pets do
    print(i, v)
end
--> 1 Cat
--> 2 Dog
--> 3 Dragon
```
The loop asks the source for 'the next one' until it says 'no more'.
tips: Use `_` for a variable you don't need: `for _, player in Players:GetPlayers()`
Breaking early is fine: `for ... do if found then break end end`
Generic for variables can't be assigned to inside the body
commonMistakes: Using `ipairs`/direct iteration on a dictionary — you'll see nothing (no array part)
Removing items from the table mid-iteration and skipping entries

examples.title: Walking players and dictionaries
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- Every player in the game
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
    print(player.Name, player.Team)
end

-- Every entry in a dictionary (order not guaranteed!)
local config = { Speed = 16, Jump = 50, Health = 100 }
for key, value in config do
    print(key, "=", value)
end
